trackedBudgets.rationale: September 22 isolated-index source candidate after removal of 129 generated previews and the unlicensed Cohere fixture. A ten percent lower bound catches incomplete exports; the ten-megabyte cap rejects new bundled binary content.
The preview-free production source candidate is 4,175,455 bytes. Ten percent lower and upper bounds catch missing content or large new assets.
A fixed 128 KiB cap provides useful headroom for four deliberately small engineering tools without permitting generated output.

September 16 release audit measured 1558353 bytes in the isolated candidate index after the chat, insertion, history and security regression additions. A 1650000-byte cap retains about six percent headroom for test source; generated outputs and model assets remain prohibited. The historical baseline is unchanged.
The September 22 scripts inventory excludes the retired 352,078-byte Cohere recording. A ten percent lower bound catches missing scripts; the existing upper cap still rejects copied artifacts.
Installer definitions remain small text inputs; 128 KiB leaves ample policy headroom without admitting built packages.

September 16 candidate measurement was 1349625 bytes including the existing rebrand and hardening plans and compiled API baseline. A 1.5-megabyte cap admits the release audit and bounded documentation growth; generated outputs remain excluded.

September 22 source candidate contains only reviewed brand and font assets. All 129 generated preview WAVs and the old manifest were removed; membership and bytes remain exact with no growth allowance.
September 22 candidate contains no Cohere health-check WAV. Bounded source and lock metadata growth remains allowed while model and audio payloads are rejected.

voicePreviews.rationale: Generated model output is excluded from source and release payloads. A selected provider creates previews in the signed-in user's bounded local cache.

releaseBudgets.rationale: Five percent upper headroom; a shrink greater than ten percent is fail-closed because it usually indicates missing self-contained or asset content.
The framework-dependent helper is small; roughly eleven percent upper headroom catches an accidental self-contained transition.
The net five-file contribution is capped at 256 KiB so shared framework files are not double-counted.
Five percent upper headroom applies only after exact App/UIAccess membership validation.
Five percent upper headroom is based on two equal-size unsigned WiX 5.0.2 builds; signing overhead is a separately measured release concern.
The larger of two accepted final measurement-command runs is the baseline because generated bundle metadata differed by 1,988 bytes; five percent upper headroom remains bounded.
This is logical validated payload size only, not compressed installer size or filesystem allocation.

releaseEvidence.repeatability: Payload files, bytes, and hashes were identical; MSI bytes were identical but hashes differed; Burn differed by 1,988 bytes. The variation is retained, not averaged.
